current_activity: Market Garden: glider elements (anti-tank battery) land north of the Neder Rijn and join the perimeter at Oosterbeek
notes: Event date: 19 September 1944, afternoon (Ellis, vol. II, pp. 38 and 49; Wikipedia: the third day of the battle). Event definition: The parachute lift of the brigade is cancelled by bad weather, but some of its gliders, carrying the anti-tank battery, land north of the river in the afternoon on landing zone L near Johanna Hoeve, while the 4th Parachute Brigade is withdrawing; the battery supports the British paratroopers at Oosterbeek. Event support: two source families (Ellis, the British official history and Wikipedia). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 38: "some of their gliders and a resupply mission flew in north of the river during the afternoon"; p. 49: "Polish gliders in the third airlift came in"; Wikipedia, 1st Independent Parachute Brigade (Poland), section Operation Market Garden: "the Brigade's anti-tank battery went into Arnhem on the third day of the battle (19 September), supporting the British paratroopers at Oosterbeek". Location: Oosterbeek, Gelderland with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is the village of Oosterbeek; landing zone L at Johanna Hoeve is about 3 km north-east of it, so precision 5 km. Location support: Wikipedia places the battery at Oosterbeek and Ellis gives the gliders landing north of the river, the zone being protected near Johanna Hoeve (p. 48). Relationship: the brigade is recorded only as attached to the 1st Airborne Division; no standing parent (such as I Airborne Corps or 21st Army Group) is recorded because no source read names one for these dates, so the validator warning about an attached entry without a standing parent is expected Commander: Major-General Sosabowski commands the brigade (Ellis, vol. II, p. 42; Wikipedia).

current_activity: Market Garden: parachuted south of the Neder Rijn east of Driel, opposite the airborne perimeter; takes Driel
notes: Event date: 21 September 1944 (Stacey, p. 314; Ellis, vol. II, pp. 38 and 53, where the OCR reads "arst" for 21st; Wikipedia). Event definition: After two days of delay by weather the brigade (2nd Battalion and elements of the 3rd, with support troops) is dropped under fire east of Driel, south of the Neder Rijn opposite the 1st Airborne Division at Oosterbeek; less than half the lift reaches the dropping zone; finding the Heveadorp ferry gone, it takes Driel and forms a defensive position there. Event support: three source families (Stacey, the Canadian official history, Ellis, the British official history and Wikipedia). Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 314: "Most of the Polish Parachute Brigade was finally dropped on the 21st south of the Neder Rijn opposite the Airborne Division's position"; Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 38: "a request that the Polish Brigade should now be landed south of the river near Driel"; p. 53: "On the arst less than half reached the dropping zone"; Wikipedia, 1st Independent Parachute Brigade (Poland), section Operation Market Garden: "the drop into Driel was delayed by two days, to 21 September"; "were dropped under German fire east of Driel. They overran Driel". Location: Driel, Gelderland (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: all three families name the drop south of the river at Driel (Stacey p. 314; Ellis pp. 38, 53; Wikipedia). Relationship: the brigade is recorded only as attached to the 1st Airborne Division; no standing parent (such as I Airborne Corps or 21st Army Group) is recorded because no source read names one for these dates, so the validator warning about an attached entry without a standing parent is expected Commander: Major-General Sosabowski commands the brigade (Ellis, vol. II, p. 42; Wikipedia).

current_activity: Market Garden: crosses the Neder Rijn from Driel by assault boat to reinforce the airborne perimeter; about 200 get over
notes: Event date: night of 23-24 September 1944 (Ellis, vol. II, p. 42; Stacey, p. 314; Wikipedia). Event definition: From Driel, joined by the 43rd Division, the Poles are given the only assault boats for a one-battalion crossing of the Neder Rijn on the night of 23-24 September; against a strong current and enemy fire only about 200 reach the airborne perimeter on the north bank. Event support: three source families (Ellis, the British official history, Stacey, the Canadian official history and Wikipedia). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 42: "only enough assault-boats were available for a one-battalion crossing and these were given to the Poles"; "only about 200 got over"; Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 314: "A few Poles and some men of the 43rd Division crossed the river on the nights of the 23rd-24th and 24th-25th"; Wikipedia, 1st Independent Parachute Brigade (Poland), section Operation Market Garden: "In total, about 200 Polish paratroopers made it across in two days". Location: Driel, Gelderland (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location approximate: the point is Driel, the start of the crossing; the men who got over joined the perimeter at Oosterbeek, about 2 km north across the river. Location support: the crossing is made from the brigade position at Driel (Ellis p. 42; Stacey p. 314; Wikipedia). Relationship: the brigade is recorded only as attached to the 1st Airborne Division; no standing parent (such as I Airborne Corps or 21st Army Group) is recorded because no source read names one for these dates, so the validator warning about an attached entry without a standing parent is expected Commander: Major-General Sosabowski commands the brigade (Ellis, vol. II, p. 42; Wikipedia). Context: the row is dated by the start of the night crossing (23 September); Wikipedia gives about 200 across in two days, Ellis about 200 on the first night.

current_activity: Market Garden: Horrocks meets Sosabowski at Driel; with 550 more men from Nijmegen, about 1,000 Poles there
notes: Event date: 24 September 1944 (Ellis, vol. II, p. 42). Event definition: General Horrocks goes forward to Driel and meets Major-General Sosabowski and Major-General Thomas (43rd Division); a further 550 men of the brigade flown in to Nijmegen have moved up, so about 1,000 Poles and three battalions of the 43rd Division are under the high south bank; Horrocks orders plans for the withdrawal of the 1st Airborne Division. Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 42: "On the 24th General Horrocks went forward to Driel and there met Major-General Sosabowski, commanding the Polish Parachute Brigade"; "a further 550 men of the Polish Brigade had been flown in to Nijmegen and moved forward to the Driel area"; "There were then about 1,000 Poles". Location: Driel, Gelderland (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Ellis p. 42 places the brigade commander at Driel on the 24th. current_activity: After Market Garden: the brigade on the south bank is ordered to march towards Nijmegen
notes: Event date: 26 September 1944 (Wikipedia). Event definition: After the withdrawal of the 1st Airborne Division across the Neder Rijn, the members of the brigade on the Allied side of the river, now including the 1st Battalion and part of the 3rd, which had been dropped near Grave on 23 September, are ordered to march towards Nijmegen; the brigade has lost about a quarter of its fighting strength. Event support: one source family (Wikipedia). Wikipedia, 1st Independent Parachute Brigade (Poland), section Operation Market Garden: "On 26 September 1944, the members of the Brigade who were on the Allied side of the Rhine (now including the 1st Battalion and elements of the 3rd Battalion, who were parachuted near to Grave on 23 September) were ordered to march towards Nijmegen". Location: Nijmegen, Gelderland with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: the point is the destination of the march, not a position reached on the day; precision 10 km covers the road from Driel to Nijmegen. Location support: Wikipedia names Nijmegen as the destination of the march ordered on 26 September.
